tagline: A Chao Phraya riverside town with a bird park, a big dam, and the old town of Sankhaburi
introHtml:
Chai Nat is a small central Thai province sitting right on the Chao Phraya River. Most people think of Chai Nat Bird Park, with its huge walk-in aviaries that let you see the birds up close, and the Chao Phraya Dam, an old water-regulating dam that has long been part of the central river plains. The town itself is small and easy to get around: pay your respects at an old riverside temple, then go see the birds or sit by the dam, all in a single day.

Head out of town toward Sankhaburi and you'll find an old town with U Thong–Ayutthaya-era temples where the old chedis and ordination halls still stand. Around Manorom and Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao there's the legend of Luang Pu Suk that draws people to come and pay respects. Chai Nat sits between Nakhon Sawan and Uthai Thani, so it's easy to stop in while passing through and string it into a Chao Phraya River-plains trip without rushing.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable — you can walk the bird park, visit temples, and sit by the Chao Phraya Dam all day without the heat

highlights.name: Chai Nat Bird Park
highlights.blurb: A bird park with huge walk-in aviaries that let you see the birds up close, with many species and a small zoo — the image people picture when they think of Chai Nat, and a must-stop

highlights.name: Chao Phraya Dam
highlights.blurb: An old water-regulating dam across the Chao Phraya River in Sapphaya district, a spot to sit by the water, look at the dam gates, and watch the fish that gather thick below the dam

highlights.name: Wat Thammamun Worawihan (Luang Pho Thammachak)
highlights.blurb: An old temple on the slope of Khao Thammamun by the Chao Phraya River, home to Luang Pho Thammachak, the town's revered Buddha image — climb up to pay respects and you'll see the river and the town below

highlights.name: Sankhaburi Old Town
highlights.blurb: An ancient town quarter with U Thong–Ayutthaya-era temples, including Wat Phra Kaeo and Wat Mahathat, where old chedis and ordination halls still remain to walk around

highlights.name: Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao (Luang Pu Suk)
highlights.blurb: A temple by the Chao Phraya River tied to the legend of Luang Pu Suk, with old mural paintings inside the wihan — a temple many devotees come to pay respects at

highlights.name: Chao Phraya riverside life and Tha Chanuan
highlights.blurb: Chai Nat is a Chao Phraya riverside town, with riverside markets and communities like Tha Chanuan where you can see everyday local life, boats, and rice fields on both banks at an easy pace

foodScene.name: Chao Phraya river fish
foodScene.note: Being a Chao Phraya riverside town, there's fresh freshwater fish — grilled, in tom yam, and deep-fried — at riverside spots and near the dam

foodScene.name: Chai Nat khao taeng kwa pomelo
foodScene.note: Chai Nat's famous pomelo variety, with crisp flesh and a sweet-tart taste — a signature local gift you can buy from orchards and roadside stalls

foodScene.name: Boat noodles and old noodle shops
foodScene.note: This is central Thailand's noodle country, with small-bowl shops serving a rich broth and long-running old noodle shops in town for an easy meal

foodScene.name: Local sweets and souvenirs
foodScene.note: Markets and shops in town have homemade Thai sweets and local souvenirs, including pomelo products to take home

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, grilled chicken, and laap are easy to find all over town and along the roads — bold flavors that hit the spot for travelers

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: A popular dinner for locals, with several places to choose from, a relaxed vibe, and friendly prices

foodScene.name: Made-to-order and roadside shops
foodScene.note: In town and along the main roads there are made-to-order shops and street food at local prices — an easy meal between sights

foodScene.name: Cafes in town and by the river
foodScene.note: There are small cafes in town and along the Chao Phraya River to sit and sip coffee after walking the bird park or visiting temples

attractions.name: Chai Nat Bird Park
attractions.blurb: A bird park with huge walk-in aviaries that let you see the birds up close, with many species, a small zoo, and space to relax — great for the whole family

attractions.name: Chao Phraya Dam
attractions.blurb: An old water-regulating dam across the Chao Phraya River at Sapphaya — walk along to see the dam gates, feed the fish below the dam, and sit by the water in the evening

attractions.name: Wat Thammamun Worawihan
attractions.blurb: An old temple on the slope of Khao Thammamun by the Chao Phraya River, home to Luang Pho Thammachak, the town's revered Buddha image — climb up to pay respects and take in the river view

attractions.name: Wat Pak Khlong Makham Thao
attractions.blurb: A temple by the Chao Phraya River tied to the legend of Luang Pu Suk, with old mural paintings inside the wihan, where many devotees stop to pay respects

attractions.name: Wat Phra Kaeo, Sankhaburi
attractions.blurb: An old temple in the ancient town of Sankhaburi, with a well-preserved U Thong–Ayutthaya-style chedi — an important historic site of the province

attractions.name: Wat Mahathat, Sankhaburi
attractions.blurb: An old temple in the heart of the ancient town of Sankhaburi, with an early Ayutthaya-era prang and chedi — traces of the old town to walk around

attractions.name: Khao Phlong–Khao Khayai
attractions.blurb: A cluster of low hills near town with viewpoints and hilltop temples — climb up for a wide view over the rice fields and the town of Chai Nat

attractions.name: Tha Chanuan riverside market and community
attractions.blurb: A riverside community quarter on the Chao Phraya that still has its trading life and local food — an easygoing place to soak up small-town riverside atmosphere

itineraryIdeas: Chai Nat 2D1N — bird park, Chao Phraya Dam, and old temples
